stem: In the nineteenth century, geology became so respected among middle-class Britons that the science came to be seen as ____, a yardstick by which other disciplines measured their scientific rigor and imaginative power.

Though McDonough discusses (i)____ the filmmaker’s aesthetic principles, it is the description of the (ii)____, the very vulgarity of the director’s films, rather than McDonough’s learned discourses on the aesthetics of the film, that makes the book so entertaining.

Saul’s particular combination of intellectuality and vitality was not paradoxical; it was category- shattering. (i)____ was, in a way, his very theme. Was ever a bookish soul so cracklingly unmediated, so (ii)____ raw life? He was as vivid physically as he was mentally, almost perversely alert, completely at home in the world of matter, repulsed by (iii)____.
Susanne Prediger argues that although rational decimals and fractions are mathematically equivalent, students generally deal with them in ____ ways, hence they are not cognitively equivalent.
Although Lemettais was ____ computer engineering, he lacked the spirit or enthusiasm to pursue it as a lifelong occupation.
In science, replicability comes with the idea that the pursuit of scientific truth should not be ____: researchers who make claims must allow others to test them empirically.
Even the most hard-nosed critics could hardly deny that the novelist’s best books are ____: they are filled with energy, imagination, and something close to a white-hot inspiration.
